back: Symptom: what is broken for users (5xx, slow requests). Cause: why (full disk, high CPU). Page on symptoms; diagnose with causes.
Latency, traffic, errors, saturation (Google SRE book, chapter 6).
Any cause, including ones nobody predicted, shows up as failed or slow requests. Cause rules only cover causes you imagined.
Predictable cliffs you cannot fix once the symptom arrives: disk full within hours, certificate expiring in days, last replica at risk.
Inactive → Pending (expression true) → Firing (true for the whole for duration). Back to Inactive when false.
Page: act within minutes. Ticket: act within days. Dashboard/log: context, nobody needs to act now.
Urgent, actionable, user-visible or imminent, requires human intelligence, and about a novel problem.
At most two incidents per 12-hour shift, because one incident with follow-up takes about six hours.
Responders stop trusting and reading alerts after too many false or unactionable ones, so real alerts get missed.
Merges alerts sharing group_by labels into one notification. Defaults: group_wait 30s, group_interval 5m, repeat_interval 4h.
Mutes target alerts while a source alert fires, e.g. hide DB connection errors while DatabasePrimaryDown fires in that cluster.
A for duration, keep_firing_for, separate fire and clear thresholds (hysteresis), longer windows.
An always-firing alert an external service expects to receive; if it stops arriving, the alerting pipeline is broken and someone is paged.
Share of pages that led to real action. 4 actionable of 20 = 20%; fix, demote or delete the rest.
User impact, how to confirm, mitigations in order of safety, escalation, known causes, owner and last-reviewed date.
